newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercials, commission.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercials, commission.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on commercial, commission and local selling, traders said.

"Locals sold all day, there was no commercial buying interest and they were selling on the close and commission houses sold," a trader said. Nov-Jan spread at $5, May-July at $2.50, Nov-May $9. November futures crush margin rose to -36.06 from Thursday's close at -40.95. Volume was 6,920 lots.
Japan bought 1,000-2,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
November canola lost $3.30 to $402.70, January fell $2.60 to $407.50. November flax lost $0.50 to $362 on commercial selling and light hedges. Feed peas did not trade.

November western barley fell $2.30 to $143.80 as Alberta Wheat Pool liquidated its long position, Richardson Greenshields bought February down $2 at $144. Nov-May spread at even money, Nov-Mar at $0.50, traders said. December feed wheat futures fell $3.90 to $167.10 March fell $2.50 to $166. Dec-May $0.50.
"The Wheat Board's Pool Return Outlook is bearish on this market but I think we took some of that into account yesterday," a trader said.
The CWB October PRO lowered feed barley by C$7 a tonne, milling and feed wheat by C$10-16 a tonne Thursday.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
